title: SolFS: An Operation-Log Versioning File System for Hash-free Efficient Mobile Cloud Backup
problem: Cloud backup on resource-limited mobile devices consumes excessive CPU for delta synchronization because identifying modified data ranges requires intensive hash computation across entire files.
motivation: Mobile cloud backup is widely used to safeguard user data, but current implementations waste valuable device resources on redundant hashing operations.
method: SolFS tracks write operation logs (offset and length) in per-file extent trees to identify changed data without hashing. It implements operation log persistence and versioning for multi-application support, uses compact logs and dynamic granularity for overhead reduction, and deploys server-side shadow files to accelerate file reconstruction.
key_novelty: Hash-free delta identification by recording write operation metadata at the filesystem level rather than computing file content hashes.
contributions: Per-file mergeable operation logging using extent trees to track write operations efficiently
Multi-tenant versioning mechanism enabling independent cloud backup application version management
Compact log and dynamic granularity optimizations reducing memory and storage overhead
Server-side shadow file mechanism reducing file reconstruction latency by up to 78%

metrics.speedup: 88.8% total cloud synchronization time reduction; 90% server-side computation overhead reduction; 78% file reconstruction latency reduction

limitations: Limitations and applicability beyond mobile cloud backup not discussed.
primary_theme: Efficient data synchronization through operation-log tracking
